rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 7 (search_right) scored 38.6396, identical to iteration 6 (last_direction) to four decimals on every track and metric. Slalom still shows 0.8 line-loss events per trial and max_error 0.0648, so the loss-recovery direction does not change the trajectory. Either last_direction already resolved to the same sign at every loss, or the line is lost only after the robot has already left the track. Either way, the recovery direction is not the lever. Across iterations 0 to 7, max_error has stayed pinned at 0.060 to 0.065 under changes to kp, kd (0.05 to 0.30), ki, sensor size, span, base_speed (1.1 to 1.6) and y (0.02 to 0.05). Iteration 5 showed that y = 0.02 hurts slalom progress, so it is rejected. Off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4). Even at the maximum body_width of 0.18 m the limit is 0.0575 to 0.06, so body width cannot help.

Change. Following the approved contingency for a max_error that stays near 0.061 under either search direction, I keep iteration 7 exactly (kd 0.30, ki 0.4, kp 2.0, y 0.05, wide span x = -0.07 to 0.07 m, 16 mm sensors, search_right) and lower controller.base_speed from 1.1 to 0.9. Speed is the remaining candidate for the start or bend-entry transient, which the feedback names as the likely driver. Iteration 4 (1.4 to 1.1) moved max_error very little, so the expected effect is small. A lower base_speed should reduce yaw overshoot and wheel slip at entry, which could bring max_error under 0.06 on the slalom and s-bend.

Expected result. max_error falls to 0.060 or below on at least one development track, and progress rises above the iteration-7 values (oval 0.115, s-bend 0.052, slalom 0.108). Risk: lower speed gives less progress per second, so progress may not rise even if the excursion shrinks. Completion is unlikely at either speed, so the score depends mainly on progress and on staying on the line longer.

Hypotheses. H1: the start or bend-entry transient is speed-driven, so 0.9 reduces max_error below 0.06. H2: max_error stays at 0.061 or above at 0.9, which points to the motor mismatch or the geometry (wheel_track, mass), not speed or the feedback loop. Next I would test wheel_track or mass, which have never been varied.

Measurements wanted: max_error, rms_error and line_loss_events per track to test H1 and H2, plus progress, completion_time and steering_oscillation to check that the speed change does not add jitter or stall the run.
